steps.title: The small words that connect things
body: This lesson covers three sets of everyday connecting words: "this / that", the endings that mean "my / your / his / her", and the common prepositions.
All the examples use nouns you already know.

steps.title: "This"
body: هَذَا points at something masculine, هَذِهِ at something feminine.
Before an indefinite noun they make a sentence: هَذَا كِتَابٌ — "This is a book."
Before a definite noun they just mean "this …": هَذَا الْكِتَابُ — "this book".

steps.title: "My", "your", "his", "her"
body: Possession is an ending on the noun, not a separate word: ـِي (my), ـكَ (your, to a man), ـكِ (your, to a woman), ـهُ (his), ـهَا (her).
كِتَابٌ (a book) → كِتَابِي (my book). A noun with one of these endings is already definite, so it takes no الـ and no tanwīn.

steps.title: "in", "on", "from", "to"
body: The common prepositions are فِي (in), عَلَى (on), مِنْ (from), إِلَى (to), مَعَ (with), plus بِـ and لِـ which attach to the next word.
The noun after a preposition changes its ending to ـِ (with الـ) or ـٍ (without): فِي الْبَيْتِ — "in the house".

steps.title: Read them aloud
steps.intro: Nine short sentences using these connecting words. Tap 🔊 to hear each one, then reveal the meaning.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.prompt: Why هَذِهِ and not هَذَا here?

options.label: بِنْت (girl) is feminine, so the demonstrative is feminine too
هَذِهِ is used at the start of every sentence
هَذِهِ means "these", pointing at more than one

steps.explanation: هَذَا and هَذِهِ agree with the gender of the noun. بِنْت is feminine → هَذِهِ.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.prompt: Why does الطَّاوِلَةِ end in ـِ, not ـُ?

options.label: It follows the preposition عَلَى, which puts the noun in the genitive (ـِ)
Feminine nouns always end in ـِ
It is a spelling mistake for ـُ

steps.explanation: A noun right after a preposition takes the genitive ending — ـِ when it has الـ.

steps.title: Nicely done
steps.message: You can now recognise هَذَا / هَذِهِ, the possessive endings, and the core prepositions with their genitive ending. Review them to keep them fresh.
